prompt: What does Harbor City's free learn-to-swim program offer, and what were its summer 2026 results?

sources.S1: Harbor City offers free learn-to-swim lessons to children aged 4 to 12 at 6 public pools. Each session runs 8 classes over 4 weeks, with classes held twice a week for 40 minutes each. Class sizes are capped at 6 children per instructor. Instructors are certified city lifeguards who receive a $3 per hour pay supplement for teaching. Priority registration is given to children enrolled in the free or reduced-price school lunch program; remaining spots open to all residents 7 days later. The 2026 budget of $185,000 is funded 70% by a state drowning-prevention grant and 30% by the city's recreation fund. Children who miss 3 or more classes are not eligible for a completion certificate. Sessions run from June through August; no lessons are offered in the fall.
sources.S2: A total of 1,920 children enrolled across all Harbor City learn-to-swim sessions in summer 2026, up from 1,350 in 2025. Of enrolled children, 1,510 completed a session. Instructors assessed children at the first and last class; 68% of completers advanced at least one skill level. Waitlists reached 430 children at the end of June. Parents of 240 children answered a voluntary survey, and 91% of them rated lessons as good or excellent. The aquatics division suggested that the lessons 'may contribute' to water safety but noted no local drowning data were analyzed. Staff recommended adding a fall session at 2 indoor pools; the parks board will consider it in November.

writer.markdown:
# Question: What does Harbor City's free learn-to-swim program offer, and what were its summer 2026 results?

## Answer
Harbor City provides free swim lessons for children aged 4 to 12 at six public pools [S1]. Enrollment rose by more than half between 2025 and 2026 [S2].

## Evidence
- Each session consists of eight 40-minute classes held twice weekly over four weeks [S1].
- That adds up to 320 minutes, or 5 hours and 20 minutes, of instruction per session [S1].
- Classes are capped at 8 children per instructor [S1].
- Instructors are hired from a contracted private swim school [S1].
- Lifeguards who teach get an extra $3 an hour [S1].
- Lessons are reserved exclusively for children in the free or reduced-price lunch program [S1].
- The state grant covers $55,500 of the budget [S1].
- The city's recreation fund contributes $55,500 [S1].
- Children who miss 2 or more classes cannot receive a completion certificate [S1].
- About 79% of enrolled children completed a session [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- 68% of all enrolled children advanced at least one skill level [S2].
- 91% of participating families rated the lessons good or excellent [S2].
- The division did not analyze local drowning data, so any water-safety effect remains unconfirmed [S2].
- A fall session at two indoor pools has been approved [S2].
- Waitlists hit 430 children by the end of June [S2].
- Most waitlisted children live in neighborhoods without a public pool.

## Next actions
- Ask the aquatics division for completion rates by pool before the parks board's November review (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Harbor City Aquatics Division, "Learn-to-Swim Initiative" (2026-04-20)
- [S2] Harbor City Aquatics Division, "Summer 2026 Learn-to-Swim Results" (2026-09-12)
